errors.quote: the repair costs $O(Vp^{O(1)}2^{-K})=o(V)$, because $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ beats every power of $p$
errors.problem: K = Theta(p^{eps c}) is itself a small power of p and does not beat every power of p. What exceeds every fixed power of p is 2^K, because K/log p -> infinity (the paper: K/log p -> infinity, and K = Theta(p^{eps c}) with eps c > 0).

errors.quote: each costing $O(VK^\tau)$ by [Fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md). The total is $O(p/K)K^\tau=O(pK^{\tau-1})$.
errors.problem: The total cost is O(V pK^{tau-1}). O(p/K)K^tau is the total after dividing by V; the paper says 'so the normalized total is'.

errors.quote: Each move peels one excess bit, exchanges the equal-width parts and restores it
errors.problem: The paper peels a single excess bit only 'when widths differ by one'. Equal-width axis moves need no peeling.

errors.quote: A visit touches $O(T/r)$ records, so $O(p^C)$ address work per record sums to $O(Tp^{A+C}/r)$
errors.problem: The paper bounds the records by O(T/r) only 'at a layer or synthetic-transform visit that processes polynomial records'. The general address swap also covers one-bit payloads, which have no polynomial suffix; their descriptor work is bounded separately by (log(2V_0))^{O(1)} = O(V_j).
An exchange costs O(VK^tau) instead of O(VK), so it saves a factor K^{1-tau}: its cost is multiplied by K^{-(1-tau)}. As written, the saving and the resulting cost factor are confused.

errors.quote: Let $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ be the volume, the number of stored bits of $T$ coefficients of $p$ bits
errors.problem: The paper's coefficient formats use Theta(p) bits per coefficient, so a padded array has Theta(V) stored bits. V = Tp is a normalization, not the exact number of stored bits.
